transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I guess the main thing is... I'm just having a little trouble staying on track with things? It's probably not a huge deal, but I tend to get pulled away by every little sound or thought. Like, if I'm trying to work on a job application or something, a car will go by outside, or my phone will light up, or... or I'll just have some random idea, and it just sends me somewhere else entirely before I even notice I stopped working. 

Um, does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with staying focused and getting distracted? Has this been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this more of a recent problem?

Um, well... I guess I've always been a little bit, you know, easily side-tracked? But I always managed okay! It wasn't really a problem when I was younger. It's really only been *this* disruptive for... I'd say about a year and ten months? Give or take? 

I had a soccer injury back then, and it kind of just... knocked me out of my usual routine. Once I lost that structure, things just got a bit harder to manage on my own. I hope it's okay that I waited this long to come in, I really thought I could just push through it and get back to normal myself. I didn't want to waste anyone's time. 

Is... is that a normal thing to happen? Like, a change in routine making it harder to focus? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of timeline.
Around the time of your soccer injury and when you noticed this change in your ability to focus, did you also experience any changes in your mood—like feeling sad, empty, or more anxious than usual?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely wasn't thrilled about being hurt and not playing, but... I wouldn't say I felt sad or empty, or anything like that. I'm usually a pretty upbeat guy! 

I guess maybe I felt a tiny bit anxious about when I'd get better, but just the normal amount, you know? Nothing extreme. I really try to look on the bright side of things. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to be helpful.

Just to clarify the timeline: before your soccer injury about a year and ten months ago, were you able to focus and stay on task without much difficulty, or do you remember struggling with distractibility even back then?

Um, well... I guess if I really think about it, I might have had a little bit of trouble back then, too? But honestly, I always thought it was just normal kid stuff! 

Like, even in elementary school, my teachers were always, um, moving my seat around. I guess I was a little chatty? I'd talk out of turn sometimes, or, you know, I'd forget to bring my homework in. And I guess I did tend to rush through my worksheets and make some careless mistakes. But I wasn't trying to be a bad student or anything! I just had a lot of energy, I think. 

I really tried my best to be good, though. Does that make sense? I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker, I really wasn't trying to be difficult.

When you were in elementary school and your teachers were moving your seat around because you were chatty—were you also physically restless or fidgety? Like, did you have trouble sitting still, or were you always on the go?

Um, I mean, I guess I was a little bit fidgety? But just, you know, normal kid energy! I wasn't running around the classroom screaming or anything like that. I always stayed in my seat when I was supposed to. 

But, um... even now, I guess I do still have a little bit of trouble staying completely still? Like, if I'm just sitting and talking with someone, my leg might be bouncing a little bit. Or I'll find myself clicking a pen, or... or just kind of messing with my keys in my pocket? 

I usually don't even realize I'm doing it until someone points it out! It's just a little habit, really. I try really hard not to be distracting to other people, though. I hope that's not too unusual? Like, a lot of people fidget a little bit, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
